title: Pressing clothes and learning instrument repair
summary: He worked in the family cleaning business and learned repair from the one music-shop repairman who treated him as an equal.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I had a great rapport with all of my teachers and everything, because I never caused anybody any problems. I was always trying to do something. And even while I was

playing music as a kid, I also cleaned and pressed clothes, like on Saturdays and sometimes in the evening. My aunt owned a cleaners and my uncle had owned a cleaners. In fact, most of the peoples from my father's...my mother's side, rather, they were involved in the cleaning and pressing business. So I learned that real early, you know. Sometimes, before I'd go to school in the morning, I'd go in and do some work, you know. And I could press clothes, knew how to clean...you know, how to clean on the machines and everything. So I had that going for me.

Also at an early age I learned how to repair my instrument. Because in Jackson, we only had one place, Mister(?) Music, and the repairman was very busy all the time repairing the band instruments from the White school, the big school -- because they had music every day in school, and a marching band, and they kept all their equipment up, you know. But the guy was very good to me, you know, and he dealt with me on a one-on-one basis, you know. Not like some little kid or the little colored kid or that... No, it was man-to-man, you know. And he was really beautiful. I never had a better friend than him, you know. He would let me come into the place and work on my instrument... In fact, I was the only one he allowed back there in his work department, where he worked, you know.

And I'd pull up a chair, get in the chair and I'd sit there, and if I'd get hung up on the instrument then he'd help me out. And he showed me all the pads and everything, cheaper than what it would have cost ordinary, you know... He really saw that I was trying to do something, and he helped me as much as he could, and gave me complete respect, you know -- for each other. And a lot of people think things like that don't happen in Mississippi, but they do. There's a lot of people that really...who will do nice things for you, you know, if they saw that you were trying to do something.
